articles.title: Dodgers - Pirates: Standings of both teams and results prior to this weekend's games
articles.standfirst: Los Angeles welcomes Paul Skenes and the rest of the Pirates at home
articles.summary: Los Angeles welcomes Paul Skenes and the rest of the Pirates at home
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers and the Pittsburgh Pirates face off this Friday at Dodger Stadium, in an interleague matchup featuring two teams heading in opposite directions.

The first pitch is scheduled for this August 21 at Los Angeles' iconic stadium , which has a capacity of 56,000 fans. The Boys in Blue come in red-hot; the Buccos are looking to pull off an upset away from home.

How do Dodgers - Pirates enter the weekend series? Latest results and standings in the table

The overall standings photo sums up the disparity. The Dodgers rank third in Major League Baseball with a record of 77 wins and 51 losses , while also leading the National League West Division. Their offensive production is one of the most fearsome in the league: 640 runs scored, just below the leader in that category, with a +145 run differential that speaks to a dominant team on both sides of the game.

On the other side, Pittsburgh is having a season of resilience. The Pirates are in 16th place overall with a record of 63 wins and 66 losses , and they are fourth in the National League Central Division. Even so, they are not a harmless opponent: they have produced 646 runs, even more than the Dodgers themselves, although their pitching (615 runs allowed) has cost them that difference that separates a contender from a middle-of-the-pack team.

The Dodgers stumbled into August — a tough stretch against the Boston Red Sox and Chicago Cubs slowed them down —, but they have regained their stride emphatically . They are coming off a sweep of the Colorado Rockies in Denver with 11-5, 7-6, and 6-4 victories, and before that they had taken care of the Kansas City Royals in a three-win series (6-5, 5-4, and 4-2). The Los Angeles bats roared back to life in Colorado, a worrying sign for any starting pitcher who comes to face them.

Pittsburgh, for its part, has shown inconsistency, but also flashes of danger. The Buccaneers closed their most recent series by winning two of three against the Detroit Tigers at home (4-1 and 4-3 after falling 5-8). Their offense is all or nothing: in recent weeks they crushed Miami 13-1 and the New York Mets 9-0, but they were also shut out and routed 0-11 by the Cubs and 1-11 by the Mets. When their pitching holds up, they can beat anyone; when it does not, blowout losses start piling up.

The matchup within the matchup: possible lineups for Dodgers - Pirates

The great attraction of this series is the Dodgers' arsenal of arms against Pittsburgh's jewel. Los Angeles rolls out a luxury rotation led by the Japanese pitchers Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Roki Sasaki , accompanied by left-handers Blake Snell and veteran Tyler Glasnow, all capable of dominating any lineup. In the bullpen, the presence of Edwin Díaz, Tanner Scott, and Blake Treinen gives Los Angeles an elite late-game finish to protect late leads.

Pittsburgh hangs much of its hopes on Paul Skenes , the 24-year-old starter who has become the reason to buy a ticket every time he takes the mound. Behind him, youngsters like Jared Jones and Bubba Chandler, along with the experienced Mitch Keller, make up a rotation with rising talent. The problem for the Buccaneers is depth: against a lineup like the Dodgers', a single stumble from the bullpen —where Gregory Soto and David... sorry, Chris Devenski stand out— can cost them the game.

Pittsburgh Offense: Ozuna, the heavy hitter

Although the Pirates do not have Los Angeles' offensive depth, they do have hitters capable of punishing mistakes. The 35-year-old Dominican designated hitter Marcell Ozuna brings power and experience to the heart of the lineup, while catcher Henry Davis and Dominican catcher Endy Rodríguez add youth behind the plate .

That production of 646 runs in the season shows that, when they connect, the Pirates can turn any game into a slugging battle.

Implications for the Playoff and World Series race

For the Dodgers, every win counts in their fight for the lead in the National League West Division , where they already hold a comfortable advantage, and in the chase for the top overall spot currently held by the Milwaukee Brewers (78-49). With only a one-game difference compared to Milwaukee in the overall standings, Los Angeles cannot afford to give away games at home against theoretically inferior opponents.

For Pittsburgh, October math is an uphill battle: with a losing record and in 16th place, the regular season has become a showcase for its young core looking ahead to the future. A victory at Dodger Stadium, however, would serve as a statement of intent for a project that is still being built around Skenes.

Players to watch during the Dodgers - Pirates

Yoshinobu Yamamoto (Dodgers) : the Japanese ace is the kind of starter who can silence Pittsburgh's offense for seven innings.

Paul Skenes (Pirates) : the number one reason not to take your eyes off the screen; his arm is capable of stealing a game from anyone, even the home favorites.

Marcell Ozuna (Pirates) : if the Pirates are going to trouble the Dodgers, his bat in key moments will be the key.

articles.title: Dodgers - Pirates Predictions: Match Favorite and Game Odds
articles.standfirst: Based on statistics and their position in the standings, the Dodgers are the favorites for the matchup
articles.summary: Based on statistics and their position in the standings, the Dodgers are the favorites for the matchup
articles.body:
There aren’t many ways to sugarcoat it: t his is a clash between a genuine World Series contender and a team fighting not to sink . The Los Angeles Dodgers are in second place in the National League and first in the West Division with a record of 77 wins and 51 losses.

On the other side, the Pittsburgh Pirates are in tenth place in the National League and fourth in the Central Division , with a 63-66 record. The difference in caliber between the two rosters is evident, and with the game being played in Los Angeles, the balance tilts even more toward the home team.

Dodgers - Pirates: Which team is favored to win and what position are they in the standings?

The heart of Los Angeles, Dodger Stadium welcomes a Pittsburgh Pirates team arriving at Chavez Ravine rowing against the current. Our read is clear and highly confident: the Dodgers impose their offensive power and elite rotation. We’re going with a 6-3 Dodgers win.

The Dodgers come in on a roll. On their most recent road trip they swept the Colorado Rockies with a devastating streak: 11-5, 7-6, and 6-4, three straight wins that reflect an offense that shows no mercy.

Overall, Los Angeles has scored 640 runs this season, one of the highest totals in the entire league, while its pitching has allowed just 495 , for a run differential of +145, the best in the National League behind Milwaukee. That balance between devastating hitting and reliable pitching is the hallmark of a contender.

The Pirates, on the other hand, live off short streaks. They are coming off taking the series against the Detroit Tigers at home (4-1 and 4-3 after falling 5-8 in the opener), which speaks to a team capable of striking when its timing is working.

Pittsburgh has scored 646 runs—surprisingly healthy production—but its problem is on the other side of the diamond: it has allowed 615, for a run differential of just +31. Its bullpen falls apart in high-leverage moments , and that, in a park like Dodger Stadium, usually comes at a high cost.

Pre-game betting market analysis for Dodgers - Pirates

The odds market for this matchup had not yet opened at the time of this analysis, s omething common when the game is one day away .

Even so, our own projection is clear-cut: given the home-field advantage, the run differential (+145 versus +31) and the superiority of the Los Angeles pitching staff, the Dodgers should open as heavy favorites on the money line.

When the board opens, we expect short prices for Los Angeles, and that's where it's worth looking at higher-value alternatives like the run line or the total.

Detailed prediction for the first Dodgers - Pirates game

We expect a game in which the Dodgers take control with early hitting. Their lineup has the depth to exploit any rough patch in the Pirates' bullpen , which has been their Achilles' heel all season.

We see Los Angeles scoring in spurts— a couple of early runs that force Pittsburgh to play from behind —and its pitching managing the lead into the final innings.

The Pirates are not harmless: with Ozuna and Davis they can hit the long ball and get closer . That’s why we’re not projecting a shutout, but rather a score with runs from both sides.

Our projected score is Dodgers 6-3, a result that reflects both the home team's dominance and the visitors' offensive ability to make the scoreline more respectable. With nine combined runs projected, the game points toward the high side (Over) on a total set around 8.5 runs, and we expect Los Angeles to cover the -1.5 run line.

Los Angeles Dodgers on the moneyline. It’s the strongest pick on the board: the superior team, at home, with a better rotation, better bullpen, and better run differential , against an opponent with inconsistent relief pitching. When the market opens, take it even at a short price.

Alternative bets for the Dodgers - Pirates

Dodgers -1.5 on the run line . If we expect Los Angeles to win convincingly and score in bunches, laying the run and a half adds value over an expensive moneyline. Ideal if you're looking for more generous odds.

Over on the total runs (around 8.5) . Pittsburgh's bullpen allows runs in bunches, and the Dodgers' offense is one of the most productive in the league. Our projected 6-3 score pushes this game over the line.

articles.title: Yankees - Blue Jays Predictions: Who will win the game and what are the odds for the matchup?
articles.standfirst: The story could be different from what happened last week in Toronto
articles.summary: The story could be different from what happened last week in Toronto
articles.body:
The New York Yankees host the Toronto Blue Jays at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx, New York, and all signs point to the home team extending their great run . With medium-high confidence, our pick is that the Yankees win the game: we’re calling it 3-1 in favor of New York.

The New York pitching has been solid and the team left Baltimore with two wins that confirm they are in their best form of the season.

What are the Yankees' and Blue Jays' standings in MLB?

The contrast in the overall MLB 2026 standings is evident. The Yankees are in sixth place with a record of 71 wins and 55 losses , and they are second in the American League East, only behind Tampa Bay.

Toronto, meanwhile, ranks 18th overall at 62 wins and 66 losses, sitting 4th in the East Division with a negative run differential of -53, one of the worst among teams with aspirations.

Recent form reinforces the trend. New York comes in having swept practically everything it has touched : wins over the Orioles by 3-1 and 5-3, and before that victories by 4-1 and 10-5 against Seattle. The Bronx Bombers have won four of their last five games.

The key piece of data, however, is the most recent head-to-head. These same teams faced each other just a few days ago in Toronto, and the Blue Jays won the first two games of that series (3-1 and 4-1) before New York responded with a 4-3 win in the finale . In other words, Toronto knows how to put the screws to the Yankees' pitching. But now the setting changes: the game is in the Bronx, where the Yankees have been especially solid.

Offensively, Toronto has shown brutal ups and downs: it thrashed Tampa Bay 10-5 and the next day lost 6-7 , then went on to win 3-1. It is a team of short streaks, not very consistent, just the opposite of the New York squad in this stretch.

Market betting analysis for the Yankees - Blue Jays

The matchup has not yet appeared on the sportsbook board at the time of writing, so there is no moneyline, total (over/under), or run line posted to cite.

When the market opens, the reading of this analysis will be clear: with the Yankees at home , in great form and with a better overall and divisional record, they should come out as clear favorites on the money line.

The value, in our opinion, will be on New York’s side to win, while Toronto’s offensive volatility opens the door to considering the -1.5 run line if the price is attractive.

Detailed forecast for the Yankees - Blue Jays game

We expect a game controlled by the Yankees, though not a walk in the park. We reset the projected score to 3-1 in favor of New York. The idea is for the home team's starting pitching to keep a Toronto offense in check that produces in spurts and that, when it cools off, barely scratches out one or two runs (just as the 1-3 and 1-4 losses New York suffered in Toronto could be repeated in reverse in the Bronx).

New York's game plan is to get ahead early and let the bullpen — with Bednar and Doval at the back end — shut the door. Toronto will have to rely on a big day from its starter to stay close ; if the game reaches the late innings with New York ahead, the depth of the home team's relief tilts the balance.

Regarding the scoring expectation, we project a game of moderate production, around 7-8 combined runs, leaning closer to an under if both starters deliver. With our 3-1, the Yankees would cover a possible -1.5 run line by a two-run margin, although that is the tightest scenario in our projection.

Yankees - Blue Jays: Main bet and alternatives for the game

Yankees on the moneyline (game winner). It is the strongest play : better record, better recent form, home-field advantage in the Bronx, and deeper pitching. We recommend it at whatever home-favorite price the market offers when it opens.

Under on the total runs (expect the line around 8.0-8.5): with top-tier starters on both sides and Toronto’s offense in intermittent mode, a low-tempo game makes sense.

Yankees run line -1.5: for those seeking better odds, backed by our prediction of a home win by two runs (3-1). It is the higher-risk option but also the one with the greatest value if the price is right.

articles.title: The World Series threats nobody wants to face in October
articles.standfirst: Among the mediocrity are several clubs with enough talent to become legitimate champions
articles.summary: Among the mediocrity are several clubs with enough talent to become legitimate champions
articles.body:
With five weeks remaining in the 2026 MLB season, the contenders are beginning to separate themselves from the pack. The Los Angeles Dodgers, Milwaukee Brewers, Atlanta Braves, Chicago Cubs, Tampa Bay Rays, New York Yankees, and likely the Boston Red Sox and Chicago White Sox have positioned themselves well for October.

Some will earn coveted first-round byes, avoiding the randomness of the Wild Card Series and significantly improving their championship chances. But baseball history rarely belongs exclusively to the favorites. Every October, one or two teams arrive carrying flaws, inconsistencies, and plenty of skepticism. Then they get hot at the right moment, ride a dominant pitching staff or a red-hot lineup, and suddenly find themselves playing for a championship.

This year's playoff bubble is crowded with teams that have spent much of the season frustrating their fan bases. Yet among the mediocrity are several clubs with enough talent to become legitimate World Series threats, if they can first secure a postseason berth. Here are six teams that shouldn't be dismissed.

Philadelphia Phillies: Built for October

Among the teams outside the elite tier, the Phillies may have the strongest case for a deep postseason run. Philadelphia's season has felt like a roller coaster. At various points, the club looked destined for disappointment. Yet a recent surge, including 13 wins in 18 games, has helped create breathing room in the National League wild-card race . What makes the Phillies dangerous is their rotation.

Cristopher Sánchez, Jesús Luzardo, and Zack Wheeler can match up with almost any playoff staff in baseball. In a short series, elite starting pitching can neutralize even the most explosive offenses. The addition of Luis Arraez has also provided much-needed balance to a lineup that too often relied on home runs and big swings.

The biggest question remains the bullpen. Philadelphia's championship hopes could ultimately hinge on setup men Orion Kerkering and Jonathan Bowlan holding late-game leads against elite competition. That's a nerve-racking formula, but one that still gives the Phillies a legitimate chance to win it all.

Toronto Blue Jays: The defending AL champs are heating up

The Blue Jays have spent much of the season flying under the radar. Much of the attention has centered on Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s inconsistent production, but Toronto's resurgence has coincided with the return to form of catcher Alejandro Kirk. After missing 62 games with a fractured thumb, Kirk is once again playing at an elite level.

Over his last 17 games, he's hitting .393 with a 1.074 OPS, helping fuel a remarkable 13-4 stretch. The quality of those wins is equally impressive. Toronto has taken series from Boston, Houston, St. Louis, Philadelphia, Tampa Bay, and New York during its recent run.

General manager Ross Atkins also managed one of the more intriguing trade deadlines in baseball. While the Blue Jays dealt Kevin Gausman and reliever Jeff Hoffman, they acquired an extra year of control with José Soriano while retaining key contributors such as closer Louis Varland . The defending American League champions haven't inspired much fear this season. Now they suddenly look like the team nobody wants to face.

San Diego Padres: Finally looking like themselves

The Padres spent the first half of the season searching for offense. Now they can't stop scoring. Since the All-Star break, San Diego is 20-12 and ranks second in the majors in runs scored during that stretch, averaging more than five runs per game. Manny Machado and company have finally found consistency at the plate, and the lineup is producing at the level many expected before Opening Day.

Just as importantly, trade-deadline acquisition Casey Mize appears to be settling into the rotation. The former No. 1 overall pick has allowed only two runs across his last 12 innings. The Padres have also accumulated valuable playoff experience. If they qualify, it would mark their fourth postseason appearance in five years and third consecutive trip. At some point, experience matters. San Diego may be reaching that point.

Arizona Diamondbacks: Dangerous and overlooked

Arizona remains one of the toughest teams in baseball to evaluate. Much depends on the health of All-Star second baseman Ketel Marte, whose knee issues have once again become a storyline. If Marte returns healthy, however, the Diamondbacks could become a nightmare matchup. The biggest reason is their pitching.

Eduardo Rodriguez has quietly emerged as one of the National League's most effective starters, posting a 2.71 ERA while logging nearly 150 innings. Brandon Pfaadt has transformed his season after a mid-year demotion, going 7-0 with a 1.79 ERA over his last 10 starts.

Arizona's offense lacks overwhelming power, but the Diamondbacks excel at something increasingly rare in modern baseball: putting the ball in play. Their low strikeout totals create pressure, extend innings, and make them particularly dangerous against high-strikeout postseason staffs. That style may not be flashy. It can still win playoff games.

Seattle Mariners: Impossible to trust, impossible to ignore

No team in baseball generates more frustration than the Mariners. Every time Seattle appears ready to make a move, it stumbles. Every time expectations disappear, the club flashes enough talent to keep hope alive.

Despite a disappointing season, the Mariners remain within striking distance of both the AL West title and a wild-card spot. The reason is simple: pitching. Seattle's rotation still ranks among the best in baseball, leading the majors in innings while placing near the top in WHIP and strikeouts.

The arrival of top prospect Kade Anderson could provide a late-season boost, while Cal Raleigh remains capable of carrying the offense for stretches. The Mariners continue to give fans reasons not to believe. Yet a team with elite starting pitching is never completely out of the conversation.

articles.title: Alex Rodriguez's passionate plea to MLB comes with a strong endorsement of Rob Manfred
articles.standfirst: A-Rod is truly a fan of where the sport of baseball is at, despite external concerns.
articles.summary: A-Rod is truly a fan of where the sport of baseball is at, despite external concerns.
articles.body:
For the most part, baseball is in a pretty good spot. There was a period of time where it seemed like many fans simply stopped caring about the sport, but MLB has rebounded in a rather strong way as of late.

That's thanks to a lot of factors, but perhaps the most important of those have been the rules changes that MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred has helped implement. Despite being kind of a punching bag among baseball fans, rules changes like the pitch clock have played a big role in helping baseball retain popularity.

Alex Rodriguez is a big Rob Manfred fan due to the resurgence of MLB

Not many want to admit that, but former MVP Alex Rodriguez isn't afraid to say it. "A-Rod" recently appeared on the " Traina Thoughts " podcast and had great things to say about Manfred . The comments came as a result of a discussion into ongoing CBA negotiations between MLB and the MLPBA .

I’m hopeful that there’s not (games missed). But I’ve spoken to dozens of people from both sides, and they’re both dug in like I’ve never seen before in 35 years of being around the game of baseball at the Major Leagues. I hope cooler heads prevail. The game is doing so well from viewership to people going to the stadiums, all the great work Rob Manfred has done with the clock, with the bases, with the shift. The product is really good right now. A World Series that saw 53 million people watch.

Rodriguez believes the league losing out on games next season due to an inability to come to agreement on a new CBA would be truly detrimental to the league. He reiterated that, " No matter how good the deal is for either side, if there is a work stoppage, it’s not going to be better than if they get a deal with no stoppage ."

articles.title: Elly De La Cruz saves injured bird before homering against the Brewers
articles.summary: Cincinnati Reds shortstop Elly De la Cruz saved an injured bird who was stuck in the diamond during a game against the Milwaukee Brewers at Great American Ball Park. The bird parked on the infield grass in Reds starting pitcher Brady Singer's line of vision.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Reds shortstop Elly De la Cruz saved an injured bird who was stuck in the diamond during a game against the Milwaukee Brewers at Great American Ball Park. The bird parked on the infield grass in Reds starting pitcher Brady Singer's line of vision.

Timeout was called, and the injured animal was surrounded by Singer, umpire Chris Guccione and a Reds bat boy, but the bird struggled to take flight.

The bat boy made an ill-fated attempt to shoo the bird off the field with his helmet. Fortunately for the bird's safety, he whiffed. Singer was also about to try to rid of the bird with his glove.

Suddenly, De La Cruz emerged from the dugout and like the shortstop he is, took command of the situation like on a routine pop-up. He called off Singer and the bat boy before he managed to scoop up the bird in his batting glove-covered hands and took it off the field.

articles.body:
An MLB National Anthem performance suddenly turned awkward when trumpeter Jesse McGuire’s instrument stopped working in front of thousands of fans.

McGuire was performing before the Arizona Diamondbacks faced the New York Yankees when his trumpet failed halfway through the song. After trying unsuccessfully to fix it, he grabbed the microphone and began singing the rest of the anthem while still holding the instrument.

The Chase Field crowd joined in before giving McGuire a standing ovation. Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo even congratulated him afterward. The moment was especially fitting because McGuire had performed during Arizona’s 2001 championship run, which the team was celebrating that night.

articles.title: What teams are in the MLB playoffs 2026 and which ones are just one win away to qualify? This is the playoff picture
articles.standfirst: Here’s where the 2026 playoff races stand with five days left
articles.summary: Here’s where the 2026 playoff races stand with five days left
articles.body:
With only five days remaining in the 2026 MLB regular season, the postseason field is beginning to take shape, although several important races remain undecided.

Six teams have already secured playoff berths: the Tampa Bay Rays, New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox in the American League, along with the Milwaukee Brewers, Los Angeles Dodgers and Atlanta Braves in the National League.

The Rays have already clinched the AL East and the American League’s No. 1 seed. In the National League, Milwaukee, Los Angeles and Atlanta have all secured their respective division titles. That leaves several teams battling for the remaining postseason places, while others are still competing for better seeding and the valuable first-round bye.

The current AL playoff field has the Rays, Cleveland Guardians and Houston Astros positioned as division winners. The Yankees, Red Sox and Chicago White Sox currently hold the three wild-card places.

Cleveland has a one-game advantage over Chicago in the AL Central, while Houston and Texas are tied at the top of the AL West. The Astros own the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Rangers, giving them the edge if the clubs finish with identical records.

In the NL, the Brewers, Dodgers and Braves have already won their divisions. The Chicago Cubs, Philadelphia Phillies and San Diego Padres currently occupy the three wild-card positions.

Those three clubs are tied, creating one of the closest races entering the final week. Arizona remains four games back and still has a mathematical path into the postseason.

Which teams can clinch Wednesday?

Several contenders can officially secure playoff spots Wednesday, depending on the results of other games. Cleveland can clinch a postseason berth by defeating Boston if Texas loses to the New York Mets. The Guardians can also qualify if they beat Boston and Houston loses to Seattle.

The White Sox can clinch with a victory over Kansas City combined with a Texas defeat. The Dodgers can secure no worse than the National League’s No. 2 seed with a win against San Diego or an Atlanta loss to Cincinnati.

Meanwhile the Cubs can punch their ticket by beating Miami or if Arizona loses to Colorado. San Diego has a more complicated route: the Padres need to defeat the Dodgers while Arizona also loses to Colorado. Philadelphia can likewise clinch with a win over Milwaukee and an Arizona defeat.

The postseason format adds another layer to the standings. The two division winners with the best records in each league receive byes through the Wild Card Series and home-field advantage in the Division Series.

The third division winner hosts the lowest-seeded wild card, while the remaining wild-card clubs meet in best-of-three series beginning Sept. 29. The Division Series is scheduled to start Oct. 3.

Tiebreakers could become crucial during the final days. MLB no longer uses a separate tiebreaker game for postseason qualification.

Instead, ties are settled mathematically, beginning with head-to-head records. With several races separated by only a few games, the final stretch could significantly reshape both the playoff bracket and the order of the seeds.

articles.title: MLB Playoffs 2026 Calendar: Key dates, and complete schedule for every game and round
articles.standfirst: Twelve teams enter the playoffs, with the World Series beginning October 23
articles.summary: Twelve teams enter the playoffs, with the World Series beginning October 23
articles.body:
Baseball’s longest season is about to become a sprint. The 2026 MLB regular season concludes Sunday, and the postseason begins only two days later on Tuesday, September 29, when four best-of-three Wild Card Series open the road to the World Series.

Twelve teams qualify, six from each league. The top two division winners in the American League and National League receive first-round byes, while the remaining eight clubs enter the Wild Card round.

The higher-seeded team hosts every game of those best-of-three series. Winners advance to the best-of-five Division Series , followed by the best-of-seven League Championship Series and World Series .

MLB Playoffs 2026 complete schedule

- Sept. 29: Wild Card Game 1 — NL 5 at NL 4; NL 6 at NL 3; AL 5 at AL 4; AL 6 at AL 3

- Sept. 30: Wild Card Game 2 — all four series

- Oct. 1: Wild Card Game 3 — all four series, if necessary

- Oct. 3: NLDS Game 1 — NL 3/6 at NL 2; NL 4/5 at NL 1. ALDS Game 1 — AL 3/6 at AL 2; AL 4/5 at AL 1

- Oct. 4: NLDS Game 2 — both series

- Oct. 5: ALDS Game 2 — both series

- Oct. 6: NLDS Game 3 — both series

- Oct. 7: NLDS Game 4, if necessary; ALDS Game 3

- Oct. 8: ALDS Game 4, if necessary

- Oct. 9: NLDS Game 5, if necessary

- Oct. 10: ALDS Game 5, if necessary

- Oct. 12: NLCS Game 2; ALCS Game 1

- Oct. 15: NLCS Game 4; ALCS Game 3

- Oct. 16: NLCS Game 5, if necessary; ALCS Game 4

- Oct. 17: ALCS Game 5, if necessary

- Oct. 18: NLCS Game 6, if necessary

- Oct. 19: NLCS Game 7, if necessary; ALCS Game 6, if necessary

- Oct. 20: ALCS Game 7, if necessary

- Oct. 23: World Series Game 1

- Oct. 24: World Series Game 2

- Oct. 26: World Series Game 3

- Oct. 27: World Series Game 4

- Oct. 28: World Series Game 5, if necessary

- Oct. 30: World Series Game 6, if necessary

- Oct. 31: World Series Game 7, if necessary

How the 2026 postseason format works

The Wild Card round is best-of-three, with the first team to two wins advancing.

The Division Series shifts to best-of-five, with the better seed hosting Games 1, 2 and 5. The Championship Series and World Series are best-of-seven.

Home-field advantage in the World Series goes to the team with the better regular-season record, which hosts Games 1, 2, 6 and 7.

Television coverage changes by round. Wild Card games are scheduled for NBC and Peacock, while the NL Division and Championship Series are on Fox/FS1.

The AL rounds are carried by TBS and HBO Max, with the World Series on Fox and Fox One.

Road to World Series leaves little room for recovery

The schedule is especially compressed early. Wild Card teams could play three games in three days before receiving only one day off ahead of the Division Series .

The Championship Series finish no later than October 20, leaving the pennant winners at least two days before the World Series begins on October 23.

If both series end quickly, the layoff could be considerably longer. One certainty remains that if the Fall Classic goes the distance, the 2026 MLB champion will be crowned on Halloween night.

articles.title: Who is ESPN analyst Erin Kate Dolan, who is in a serious relationship with an MLB star?
articles.standfirst: The ESPN analyst made headlines again after sharing images of her behind-the-scenes life, including one with Alec Bohm.
articles.summary: The ESPN analyst made headlines again after sharing images of her behind-the-scenes life, including one with Alec Bohm.
articles.body:
E rin Kate Dolan made headlines on social media again after sharing a carousel of eight photos on Instagram. The ESPN analyst showed different moments from her daily life , from her work on television to meetings with friends and a picture alongside Alec Bohm , third baseman for the Philadelphia Phillies.

The post carried a simple message: “Behind the scenes!” . Among the images are scenes related to Sunday NFL Countdown, baseball games, and moments outside the ESPN studios. The photograph alongside Bohm was one of the most talked-about in the post.

Dolan is an analyst specializing in sports betting and one of the familiar faces of ESPN. She joined the network in December 2021 and since then has gained presence across different television programs and digital platforms. These include ESPN BET Live and Sunday NFL Countdown.

Before joining ESPN, she worked for FanDuel and PointsBet, where she was involved in sports betting-related content. She also spent time at B/R Betting and SiriusXM. Before focusing on this field, she worked as a sports reporter for PHL17 in Philadelphia and as a sideline reporter for the Philadelphia Wings.

Dolan studied television journalism at Penn State University and graduated summa cum laude in 2018. Her career allowed her to combine sports journalism with a specialization that is increasingly present at major American networks.

Erin Kate Dolan and Alec Bohm's relationship

Her personal life has also generated interest, especially since her relationship with Alec Bohm became known. Rumors about the two had circulated for months until Dolan publicly confirmed that they were together in February 2025.

“Yes, I’m dating Alec Bohm, everyone knows it,” the journalist then told The Philadelphia Inquirer. The confirmation came shortly before the New Orleans Super Bowl, which Bohm accompanied her to.

The couple has chosen to keep their relationship relatively discreet, and there are few occasions when they share pictures together. That is why each of Bohm's appearances in Dolan's posts usually draws attention among her followers.

The new photograph does not show a different side of the couple, but it does offer another glimpse into a relationship that both have preferred to keep away from constant exposure.

While Bohm continues his career as the Phillies' third baseman, Dolan has established herself as one of the faces of ESPN associated with sports betting analysis. Two different jobs, but within the same world: professional sports.

articles.standfirst: Major League Baseball’s championship showdown begins on October 23, with the American League and National League champions set to battle for the sport’s biggest prize
articles.summary: Major League Baseball’s championship showdown begins on October 23, with the American League and National League champions set to battle for the sport’s biggest prize
articles.body:
The countdown to the 2026 World Series is underway, with Major League Baseball ’s postseason moving toward its final stage.

The Fall Classic is scheduled to begin on Friday, October 23, when the American League champions face the National League winners in Game 1.

The series could last until Halloween, with a potential decisive Game 7 scheduled for Saturday, October 31. However, that final date will only be needed if neither team manages to win four games earlier in the best-of-seven contest.

MLB’s official schedule confirms that the championship could span nine calendar days, including scheduled rest days.

The teams competing for the title have yet to be determined. As the League Championship Series unfolds, the remaining clubs are fighting for the opportunity to represent their respective leagues on baseball’s biggest stage.

2026 World Series schedule: Dates for every game

MLB has released the dates for all seven potential games. The schedule includes two games at the start, a move to the opposing team’s ballpark for Games 3 and 4, and additional contests if the series remains undecided.

Here is the complete calendar, with games marked as conditional where applicable:

- Game 1 — Friday, October 23: American League champion at National League champion.

- Game 2 — Saturday, October 24: American League champion at National League champion.

- Game 3 — Monday, October 26: National League champion at American League champion.

- Game 4 — Tuesday, October 27: National League champion at American League champion.

- Game 5 — Wednesday, October 28: National League champion at American League champion, if necessary.

- Game 6 — Friday, October 30: American League champion at National League champion, if necessary.

- Game 7 — Saturday, October 31: American League champion at National League champion, if necessary.

The dates and home-team order are listed in MLB’s published postseason calendar. Specific starting times remain subject to confirmation, so fans should check the official schedule as the series approaches.

Where will the 2026 World Series be played?

The opening two games are scheduled to take place at the home ballpark of whichever league champion finishes with the better regular-season record. Games 3 and 4 will then move to the other finalist’s stadium, with the schedule alternating back if the series extends further.

That arrangement makes the regular season relevant even after the playoff field has been reduced to two teams.

Earning home-field advantage can give a club the benefit of playing in front of its own supporters at the beginning of the championship, while potentially hosting the deciding game if the matchup goes the distance.

The World Series follows a best-of-seven format, meaning the first team to collect four victories becomes MLB champion. A sweep would conclude the series after four games, while a more competitive matchup could require all seven scheduled contests.

How to watch the Fall Classic

For viewers in the United States, FOX will broadcast the 2026 World Series, with streaming available through FOX One.

FOX Sports also provides postseason coverage and updates, while MLB’s official postseason page is the place to follow the bracket, results and schedule as the playoffs progress.

Fans should check local listings and the relevant streaming service closer to each game, particularly if start times or broadcast details are updated. International viewing options may differ by country.

The stakes will be considerable for both finalists. The World Series represents the final hurdle after the Wild Card Series, Division Series and League Championship Series, and it gives the two remaining teams the chance to turn a successful season into a championship.

With Game 1 set for October 23 and a possible Game 7 on October 31, baseball fans can already mark the key dates in their calendars. Whether the title is decided quickly or comes down to the final night, the Fall Classic will bring the 2026 MLB season to its conclusion.

articles.title: Cleveland Guardians break Travis Kelce’s heart once again: Their MLB curse has now lasted 78 years
articles.standfirst: Díaz, Caminero and Peralta lead Rays to 7-3 win over Guardians and a trip to the World Series
articles.summary: Díaz, Caminero and Peralta lead Rays to 7-3 win over Guardians and a trip to the World Series
articles.body:
For yet another season, Cleveland baseball fans will have to wait.

The city’s proud major league franchise still hasn’t won a World Series since 1948.

After the Guardians fell a little short once again with a 7-3 loss to Tampa Bay in Game 6 of the American League Championship Series on Monday night, it will be the Rays meeting the Milwaukee Brewers in the Fall Classic — the first once since 1980 between teams seeking their first World Series title.

“Yeah, let it hurt,” Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt said he told his club. “That hurts. I couldn’t be more proud of our group. It just hurts. It stings. Really felt like we had a team to go and just weren’t able to get there.”

Seemingly in control of the best-of-seven ALCS after winning two of the first three games, José Ramírez and the Guardians are left to lament three straight losses. Tampa Bay used clear superiority in its starting rotation, bullpen and late-series offense to eliminate Cleveland.

Seeing the Guardians’ best relievers repeatedly – including opener Shawn Armstrong in Game 4 on Saturday and again Monday in Game 6 — the Rays improved their swings as the series progressed.

Cleveland’s staff, which struck out 27 batters over the first three games, didn’t get its first strikeout Monday until Daniel Espino fanned Victor Mesa Jr. in the fifth inning.

By then, Tampa Bay held a 3-0 lead, grinding out runs in trademark fashion. And, as they did over the prior two games, the Rays' pitching staff kept the Guardians at arm’s length.

“It just seemed like when we had the hit that we wanted, just runners weren’t where they needed to be,” designated hitter Jo Adell said. “That’s the name of the game. And they threw the ball well. I give credit where credit's due. They did a phenomenal job throwing the baseball and playing their game and we came up short. We weren’t able to match that.”

The Guardians nearly matched it in the eighth, when they almost overcame a 5-1 deficit. Chase DeLauter was initially ruled out on a grounder, but Cleveland challened and the call was overturned after a replay review, giving the rookie his second hit of the game. After Nathaniel Lowe's single, Rays manager Kevin Cash brought in struggling left-hander Ian Seymour, who promptly loaded the bases by walking Travis Bazzana.

Seymour then walked Patrick Bailey to score DeLatuer, and hit Angel Martínez with a pitch to force in Lowe and make it 5-3.

But with the bases still loaded, Kevin Kelly entered and struck out Brayan Rocchio on three pitches.

“We fought every pitch,” Bazzana said. “We went down 5-1 and fought back when it looked like it was over. Obviously, that’s not good enough to get it done, but that just shows some of the character that we have in this clubhouse.”

Cleveland led the AL with 41 comeback victories this season, but fatigue clearly caught up with the Guardians as Tampa Bay closed out the series. The Guardians didn’t hold a lead over the final 25 innings.

And Vogt was left wondering whether ace Gavin Williams, who struck out nine over five innings in his Game 3 victory, would’ve been the better option Monday on three days’ rest.

Instead, the manager used eight relievers Monday, and Tampa Bay showed no hospitality.

The Rays even got to Cleveland’s best reliever, All-Star closer Cade Smith, when the right-hander faced Junior Caminero in the seventh. Caminero pulled Smith’s first-pitch splitter off the left-field foul pole for a two-run homer that gave the Rays a 5-1 lead.

Yandy Díaz added a two-run shot off Hunter Gaddis to make it 7-3 in the eighth.

“That's a great baseball team,” Guardians outfielder Steven Kwan said. “Great baseball teams win big games. They played defense better than us, hit better than us, they pitched better than us. We didn’t beat ourselves. We got beat. So, as a competitor, I think we can live with that. Disappointing, but that’s a great team over there.”

Cleveland, which won the AL Central and came back to beat the Chicago White Sox in their Division Series by winning three straight, has advanced to the World Series four times since winning its most recent title by beating the Boston Braves in the 1948 World Series.

The Rays even got to Cleveland’s best reliever, All-Star closer Cade Smith, when the right-hander faced Junior Caminero in the seventh. Caminero pulled Smith’s first-pitch splitter off the left-field foul pole for a two-run homer that gave the Rays a 5-1 lead.
Yandy Díaz added a two-run shot off Hunter Gaddis to make it 7-3 in the eighth.

“That's a great baseball team,” Guardians outfielder Steven Kwan said. “Great baseball teams win big games. They played defense better than us, hit better than us, they pitched better than us. We didn’t beat ourselves. We got beat. So, as a competitor, I think we can live with that. Disappointing, but that’s a great team over there.”

Cleveland, which won the AL Central and came back to beat the Chicago White Sox in their Division Series by winning three straight, has advanced to the World Series four times since winning its most recent title by beating the Boston Braves in the 1948 World Series.

articles.title: Superagent Scott Boras issues serious warning to MLB teams ahead of impending lockout on December 1
articles.standfirst: With a potential salary cap and lockout approaching, baseball's biggest agent believes clubs should act before the rules change
articles.summary: With a potential salary cap and lockout approaching, baseball's biggest agent believes clubs should act before the rules change
articles.body:
The next few weeks could prove decisive for Major League Baseball 's biggest free agents, with Scott Boras warning that teams waiting for clarity on a new labor agreement may discover that the rules have changed before they can complete their deals.

Baseball's current collective bargaining agreement expires on December 1, 2026, and the growing expectation of an offseason lockout has introduced uncertainty into negotiations involving some of the sport's most valuable players.

Boras , who represents star left-hander Tarik Skubal , believes clubs should recognize an opportunity rather than allow concerns over the impending labor dispute to stall negotiations.

His argument is straightforward: teams currently possess negotiating flexibility that could disappear if owners successfully introduce restrictions on spending and contract structures.

Speaking to The Athletic, Boras urged organizations to consider how their financial options could change under a new collective bargaining agreement.

"For many teams, I can make an argument it's clearly best for them to sign players currently, before the (new) CBA, than it is after," Boras said.

"Because they have more freedom to do what they're going to do. They can react later. Now they can get the talent. They can get what they want."

The warning comes amid discussions about a potential salary cap, with one ownership proposal reportedly including a $245.3 million payroll ceiling.

Other proposals have explored limiting the length and value of contracts offered to free agents, although none of those restrictions has been agreed upon.

Boras believes that uncertainty strengthens the case for completing deals before negotiations potentially produce a different financial framework.

"In a talent-run world, there are no rules until there are rules," he said.

Skubal could become biggest test of Boras' strategy

Few players illustrate the stakes more clearly than Skubal , whose 2026 campaign strengthened his position among baseball's most sought-after pitchers.

The left-hander recorded a 12-7 record and 2.72 ERA across 158.2 innings with the Detroit Tigers and Los Angeles Dodgers , striking out 186 batters.

One executive has reportedly suggested a potential 10-year, $400 million agreement, highlighting the considerable sums involved in negotiations for elite pitching talent.

The approaching deadline could encourage teams to accelerate discussions, particularly with players willing to reach agreements before a possible transaction freeze.

"I think there's going to be more urgency," one anonymous executive told The Athletic.

Another predicted that players outside the most expensive tier could move particularly quickly. "The middle tier could move fast," the executive said.

Lockout strategy creates further uncertainty

While Boras sees an opportunity for teams to secure talent, MLB commissioner Rob Manfred has previously described an offseason lockout as a bargaining tool.

"There is leverage associated with an offseason lockout, and the process of collective bargaining under the NLRA (National Labor Relations Act) works based on leverage," Manfred said.

If owners impose a lockout, major-league signings and trades would be suspended until a new agreement is reached.

The previous work stoppage lasted 99 days, beginning in December 2021 before ending in March 2022 without canceling regular-season games.

That precedent underscores the uncertainty facing clubs and players as the deadline approaches.

Whether Boras ' warning accelerates negotiations remains unclear, but the decision facing MLB teams is becoming increasingly significant: secure expensive talent under the existing rules or risk waiting through a potentially prolonged labor dispute.

articles.title: The Brewers take the lead in the World Series with a record and VAR
articles.standfirst: Milwaukee defeats the Rays 3-2 with a controversial play in the ninth inning and a speed record by its pitcher Misiorowski: he threw the ball at 166 kilometers per hour
articles.summary: Milwaukee defeats the Rays 3-2 with a controversial play in the ninth inning and a speed record by its pitcher Misiorowski: he threw the ball at 166 kilometers per hour
articles.body:
'With smoking barbecues in the crowded parking lot of American Family Field in Milwaukee from six hours before the start of the game and an exceeded attendance of 43,250 spectators (because additional standing-room bleachers were installed), the Brewers celebrated their return to the MLB World Series 44 years later with a narrow, controversial, and record-setting victory. The 3-2 win over the Rays , who have also never won the title, lived up to expectations: two athletic teams, without huge hitters. There were no "home runs" or many "strikeouts" (eliminations of players after three strikes), but there was a historic pitch and a review of a play in the last inning that somewhat altered the fate of the game. '

'In the first inning, Jacob Misiorowski , the 24-year-old Brewers pitcher, threw the ball at 166 kilometers per hour . It is a record in the history of the World Series . Although this type of measurement has been taken since 2008 and the MLB championship final has been held in the modern era since 1903 (Boston beat Pittsburg 5-3 in a best-of-nine series format), the iron arm of the Missouri "pitcher" is golden: in September 2026 he became the first player in Major League history to throw 1,000 pitches at 160 kilometers per hour or more. Misiorowski surpassed the previous mark of 165 km/h set by Aroldis Chapman (Cubs) in the 2016 Fall Classic'

Then the Brewers' designated hitter Christian Yelich drove in two runs to make it 3-1 , and although the Rays did not give up and closed the gap on the scoreboard, everything seemed decided in the ninth inning. "Glory Days" by Springsteen was playing over the loudspeakers and the Milwaukee players were celebrating the victory when the umpires overturned a double play that seemed to seal the outcome of the game after a video review following a challenge by the Rays. By millimeters, Pratt's right foot had come off the base before fielding the ball . The typical neighborhood play, as it is known in MLB. After the scare, the Brewers then secured the win. Today the second game is being played, also in festive Milwaukee .

articles.title: Brewers comeback to take a 2-0 lead in the World Series
articles.standfirst: The Rays scored four runs in the first inning but did not score again, and by the seventh they were already trailing on the scoreboard
articles.summary: The Rays scored four runs in the first inning but did not score again, and by the seventh they were already trailing on the scoreboard
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers came back from a four-run deficit this Saturday and defeated the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4, a result that extends their lead to 2-0 in the Major League World Series.

With an 11-hit attack and an outstanding performance from its relief pitching, the Milwaukee team put its rival in a difficult situation. If they want to be champions, the Rays will now have to win four of five games, two of them on the road .

Defeated 3-2 this Friday in the opener of the series, Tampa Bay's "Rays" quickly figured out pitcher Logan Henderson and scored four runs in the top of the first inning.

Cuban Yandy Díaz reached second base on an error by shortstop Cooper Pratt ; Chandler Simpson and Dominican Junior Caminero each drove in a run with hits, and Liam Hicks drove in two with a home run.

The "Brewers" pulled two back in that very first inning against pitcher Drew Rasmussen , by stringing together singles from Venezuelan Jackson Chourio and Jake Bauers that left them stranded on the corners.

After surviving a bad fielding play by Mexican Jonathan Aranda in foul territory, Venezuelan William Contreras connected on an RBI single and Garret Mitchel drove in the second run with a hit.

From there, the pitchers took over, but the home team took advantage of the visitors' poor defense and in the fourth inning cut the deficit by one run. Cooper Pratt drew a walk, reached third base on a hit by Sal Frelick, and scored on an error by Aranda .

A home run by Frelick tied the game in the sixth inning and set everything up for the Brewers to seal the win with another run in the seventh. Brice Turang hit a double, advanced to third base on a flyout by Mitchell, and scored on a hit by Pratt.

In the ninth inning, the visitors opened with a double by De Lucca , but reliever Aaron Ashby got the Cuban players Víctor Mesa Jr. and Yandi Díaz out , and in between recorded an out against pinch hitter Ben Williamson .

For the Brewers, Frelick went 2-for-4 with a home run and an RBI; for Tampa, De Lucca went 2-for-4.

The game was won by Dominican reliever Abner Uribe, with one and one-third innings of work in which he allowed no hits , issued one walk and struck out one opponent. Tyler Wells took the loss and Aaron Ashby earned the save .

This Sunday will be a day of rest and the third game will be played on Monday. Robert Gasser will pitch for Milwaukee and Dominican Freddy Peralta for Tampa Bay.

articles.title: World Series 2026 Prize Money: How much is this year's winning team getting?
articles.standfirst: The 2026 MLB champions will receive more than the Commissioner's Trophy and World Series rings, with tens of millions of dollars available through baseball's postseason players' pool.
articles.summary: The 2026 MLB champions will receive more than the Commissioner's Trophy and World Series rings, with tens of millions of dollars available through baseball's postseason players' pool.
articles.body:
Winning the World Series is the ultimate achievement in Major League Baseball , but the champions also stand to earn a substantial financial reward.

The 2026 World Series features the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays , with both teams competing for the title and a significant share of MLB's postseason prize money.

Unlike competitions that award a fixed cash prize to the winner, MLB distributes postseason money through a shared pool funded primarily by ticket revenue from playoff games.

The World Series champions receive 36 percent of the total players' pool, while the runners-up collect 24 percent.

The exact amount for the 2026 champions has not yet been confirmed. However, last year's figures provide a useful indication of what players could earn.

In 2025, the total postseason pool reached approximately $128.2 million, with the Los Angeles Dodgers receiving $46.1 million after winning the championship.

How much money will the 2026 World Series winners receive?

Based on the previous season's distribution, the winning team could receive around $46 million or more for its share of the postseason pool, although the final figure will depend on the money generated by the 2026 playoffs.

The Dodgers ' 2025 allocation was worth $46,147,019.39. Their players voted to distribute 82 full shares, alongside 12.5 partial shares and $340,000 in additional cash awards.

A full share was worth $484,747.57, meaning eligible players receiving a full allocation earned nearly half a million dollars each on top of their regular compensation.

The individual amounts are not identical across teams. Players vote on how many full and partial shares to award, while certain other club employees can receive cash awards.

Consequently, the total allocation a team receives is different from the amount an individual player takes home.

MLB's formula also means that a seven-game World Series does not automatically guarantee a larger payout.

The pool is calculated using specified portions of ticket receipts from selected games across the Wild Card Series, Division Series, League Championship Series and World Series.

The runners-up also receive a significant financial reward. Toronto's 2025 postseason allocation was approximately $30.8 million after the Blue Jays lost to the Dodgers in the World Series. A full share for a Blue Jays player came to $354,118.39.

The two teams eliminated in the League Championship Series each received allocations of approximately $15.4 million.

For Milwaukee and Tampa Bay , the financial incentive adds another dimension to the biggest series of the baseball season.

The championship itself remains the main prize, but the postseason pool provides an additional reward for players and eligible personnel who helped their teams reach the final.

Ultimately, the 2026 champion's precise payout will only be known once MLB calculates the final pool and the winning club determines how to distribute its allocation.

Last year's figures suggest the team could receive roughly $46 million, with individual full shares potentially approaching $500,000 depending on the final calculations and the number of shares awarded.
